headline: Wall Street jumps on chip rally after another ASX loss
paragraphs: Wall Street was sharply higher around 4 am Sydney time. The S&P 500 was up 4.9% at that point; the Nasdaq-100 was up 6.6% in a separate intraday reading, as chip shares rallied after Nvidia reinstated Jensen Huang as CEO. That put tech out in front, but those gains were not closing figures.

Australia missed that bounce: the ASX 200 closed Monday down 0.26% at 8,570.56, its eighth consecutive fall. Banks weighed on the index even as miners recovered. The Aussie dollar also slipped, from US66.66¢ on Friday to US66.38¢ at the RBA’s Monday afternoon reading.

Gold and oil went in opposite directions. Spot gold rebounded 3.9% to about US$3,670 an ounce in US trading as buyers stepped in after Friday’s 14-month low. Brent fell about 3.5% to about US$89.32 a barrel as rising supply weighed on prices. Both are intraday readings.
